walkthroughs.body_html:
World History Topics (two, same as SL) — a core area of History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

World History Topics (two, same as SL) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with World History Topics (two, same as SL).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which 1938 conference ceded the Sudetenland to Germany?
options: Locarno
Munich
Yalta
Geneva

mcqs.q: Who signed the 1939 non-aggression pact for the USSR?
options: Molotov
Litvinov
Khrushchev
Beria

mcqs.q: Why did Caribbean migrants come to Britain in 1948 on the Windrush?
options: Britain faced post-war labour shortages; the 1948 British Nationality Act gave Commonwealth citizens UK residency rights and Caribbean migrants answered the call to rebuild.
The USSR collapsed because NATO invaded Moscow.
Windrush migrants came as refugees from Caribbean famines.
Windrush migrants were illegal immigrants from outside the empire.

mcqs.q: Why did the Communists win the Chinese Civil War?
options: Windrush migrants came as refugees from Caribbean famines.
Mao won because the USA refused to support the KMT.
Mao's appeal to peasants through land reform, the discrediting of the KMT by corruption and inflation, and the disciplined organisation of the PLA — not foreign aid.
Mao won because the USSR sent the Red Army to help.

mcqs.q: Why did the Soviet Union collapse in 1991?
options: The USSR collapsed because NATO invaded Moscow.
The USSR collapsed because Reagan outspent it in the arms race.
Windrush migrants came as refugees from Caribbean famines.
A combination of economic stagnation, nationalist movements in republics, the failed August 1991 coup, and Gorbachev's reforms accelerating loss of control to Yeltsin.
